newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica business confidence still falling - survey.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica business confidence still falling - survey.

text.p: Business confidence continued to decline at the end of the third quarter but growth of at least three percent was still expected this year, a survey has found.
The University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research (BER) said on Thursday that its latest survey had found that manufacturers had reported that domestic demand had declined sharply.
But overseas demand remained good and was expected to strengthen.
"This finding of a breakdown in confidence in the manufacturing sector is supported by a low level of confidence in the retail sector," BER director Ockie Stuart said.
Retailers reported that falling demand had enabled them to sell from current stocks, resulting in fewer orders being placed with manufacturers.
The confidence of motor dealers had been hit by lower motor vehicle sales.
"The sales of used vehicles were particularly bad and this situation is expected to continue," Stuart said.
Despite continued sluggish business conditions in the building sector, confidence was not affected.
"This can be ascribed to the perception that the declining trend in the building industry is busy levelling out," he said.
Despite the weaker confidence levels, Stuart said a bumper crop harvest and an improvement in exports should ensure average gross domestic product growth of at least three percent in real terms.
